question: Which statement best describes Main idea?
options: A favicon should remain recognizable when shown very small. A detailed logo may become an unreadable blur. It is like simplifying a road sign so drivers can identify it quickly. Use a simple mark, check light and dark browser themes, and provide formats and sizes supported by your deployment needs. For example, check a light and dark tab background when selecting icon contrast.

A `<link>` element in the document head can point to a favicon file. It does not appear as a visible control in the page body. It is like attaching a label to the folder rather than printing it inside the document. Make sure the path works after the site is deployed. For example, verify the icon path on a nested route, not just at the site root.

The `rel` attribute describes the relationship between the current page and the linked resource. For an icon, use the appropriate icon relationship. It is like labeling a package as a logo or stylesheet. The browser uses this hint to decide how to interpret the linked file. For example, a simplified mark remains clearer in a tab than a detailed full logo.

Use a stable file path and verify that the icon returns successfully from the deployed site. A correct local path can still break when an app is hosted beneath a subpath. It is like checking the street address after moving offices. Inspect the browser tab and network response after deployment. For example, a missing icon should not prevent page content and controls from working.
explanation: A `<link>` element in the document head can point to a favicon file. It does not appear as a visible control in the page body. It is like attaching a label to the folder rather than printing it inside the document. Make sure the path works after the site is deployed. For example, verify the icon path on a nested route, not just at the site root.
